data.sentence: Okay, I think we've got everyone — Kendra, Owen, thanks for making the time, and Ravi's joining from our engineering side.
Yeah, thanks Aisha. I brought Owen because he runs our SecOps team day to day and he's the one living with the alerts.
Hi everyone. Happy to be here, though I'll be honest, I came with a list.
That's exactly what we want. The goal today is to walk through what changed in Detect since March and then spend most of the time on your alert tuning.
Good, because the decision is in about ten days and right now SentinelShield is ahead on our scorecard.
Their demo showed pipeline health right in the console, and their SLA is ninety-nine point nine — that landed with my CFO.
Understood, and I appreciate you telling us where things stand. Ravi, do you want to start with the reliability piece?
Sure. So the short version — the March outage came from a single ingestion node with no failover, and that's gone now.
We run active-active processing nodes, there's a circuit breaker in front of the queue, and failover in our last test came in at about twelve seconds.
Twelve seconds of what, though — delayed alerts or lost events?
Delayed. Events buffer during the failover and replay in order, so nothing is dropped, you'd just see alerts a few seconds late.
Okay, that's actually a meaningful difference from March.
The other thing my board keeps asking is how we'd even know if it happened again — last time we heard about it from our own analysts.
That's fair, and it's the piece I'm most excited about. We're shipping a pipeline health panel in the Detect console in early June.
It shows ingestion lag per source, queue depth, and a heartbeat, and you can route a heartbeat-missed alert straight to PagerDuty.
If that goes to PagerDuty, that solves my biggest complaint, honestly.
Owen, can we switch to alert volume? Kendra mentioned fatigue was a problem even before the outage.
Yeah, it's been rough. We average something like a hundred and eighty alerts a day and maybe fifteen of them are worth a human looking at.
Most of the noise is from our Azure batch jobs overnight and the CloudPrime autoscaling events during sales peaks.
That pattern makes sense. Those are behavioral baselines that never learned your peak season, because you deployed right before it.
What I'd suggest is a re-baseline using April data, suppression windows for the batch jobs, and entity-level thresholds for the autoscaling groups.
Entity-level meaning I can set different thresholds for prod versus staging?
Exactly, per entity type or per tag. We ran the same exercise with a manufacturing customer last month and they went from about two hundred a day to around thirty-five.
If we got anywhere near that, my team would throw you a party.
Can we see that on our data before the decision, though? I can't take a projection to the steering committee.
Yes. If Owen can give us read access to the April alert export, we can run the tuning in a sandbox tenant and show you before-and-after numbers.
I can get that to you tomorrow.
On the commercial side, Kendra, I know the SLA was a sticking point.
We can offer an enhanced Detect SLA at ninety-nine point nine with service credits that actually scale, and we'd credit back the March incident on this renewal.
That helps. Would the health panel be in the contract or just on the roadmap?
I'll confirm with product, but I believe we can put the June date in writing as a named deliverable.
If you can get that in writing and the tuning numbers hold up, I think this becomes a much easier conversation internally.
And to be fair, Protect and Comply v2 have been great — Comply cut our PCI evidence prep by more than half.
That's really good to hear, and I'll share that with the Comply team.
One more ask — can we get the post-mortem in a format I can hand to our auditors, not just the blog version?
Yes, there's a detailed version with the timeline and control changes. I'll send it under NDA.
Great. So to recap — Owen sends the alert export, Ravi runs the tuning sandbox, and I send the SLA proposal and confirm the health panel date.
Can we hold forty-five minutes next Wednesday to review the results before your committee meets?
Wednesday works. Let's do it.
Thanks Ravi, this was a lot more concrete than I expected.
